RSTR — a groovebox for posters

Feasible. The core already runs.

Everything on this page — the samples, the phone screens, the demo below — comes from one small canvas engine written as a spike. Stills are a solved problem. Motion works in the engine; getting it out as an MP4 on the phone is the one thing that needs a device test. Photo backgrounds are routine. It is a rule-based generator, not AI image generation: it never invents a photograph, it composes type, colour and geometry inside rules.

04How it works

A design is a small piece of data. The image is never stored; it is redrawn from this, at any size, still or moving. That is the modular identity system: three independent seeds, so you can lock the colour and reroll the layout, or keep the motif and change the format.

{ "style":  "swiss",
  "format": "3:4",
  "seeds":  { "layout": 166300, "colour": 2199312, "motif": 27293894 },
  "motif":  "topo",        // or null = seed decides
  "palette": 4,            // or null = seed decides
  "text": { "title":    { "on": true,  "v": "Signal and noise" },
            "subtitle": { "on": true,  "v": "A modular identity system" },
            "info":     { "on": true,  "v": [ ... ] },
            "caption":  { "on": false, "v": "" } } }
  • Rule set = a function that turns that data into a layout. Swiss: 6-column grid, one margin, one rhythm unit, one accent, flush-left type. Postmodern: jittered lattice, tilted strips, drop shadows, pattern ground.
  • Motif = a drawing routine that fills a grid-aligned box: topographic contours, colour blocks, diagonal bars, dot gradient, disc. Each takes a time value, so each one animates for free.
  • Text slot = title, subtitle, info (up to 3 label/value pairs), caption. Off slots give their space back to the motif. Session 5 turns these into layers you add, remove and rank.

05Feasibility, line by line

PieceCallWhy
Stills: JPEG / PNG at 1:1, 3:4, 9:16YESDone in the spike. Canvas export, on the phone, offline.
Random within rules, locks, reproducible seedsYESDone in the spike.
Text slots on/off, auto-fitYESDone. Info slot needs a proper editor.
Animation previewYESDone (Motion toggle above). Topo is the heavy one; fine on your phone class, untested there.
MP4 export on the phoneTESTChromium's MediaRecorder gained MP4 with H.264 (Chromium intent-to-ship), but it records in real time. Frame-exact export means WebCodecs plus an MP4 muxer. First row of the motion phase is a device test. Fallback: WebM, or frames rendered in a chat.
Upload a photoYESOne photo; Shuffle moves, scales and crops it. Monochrome, duotone, halftone, threshold, posterise, dither, and the finishes. Stays on the phone. Session 4.
Choose export size and file typeYESJPEG, PNG, WebP at 1×, 2×, 3×. 3× needs a test on your phone.
JPEG printable up to A3TESTNeeds a fourth format (1:√2) and a 3508 × 4961 px render, about 17 megapixels. Type and graphics stay crisp; a photo is only as sharp as the photo. RGB only, so neons print duller. Memory on the phone is the thing to test; strips are the fallback.
Mix two stylesLATERSession 6, experimental, Advanced only. Some pairs will cross well, some will not.
Add, remove and rank text layersLATERSession 5. Replaces the four slots, so it carries a migration.
More movements (Bauhaus, Brutalist, …)YESOne rule set is roughly one build chat. Quality depends on how tight the rules are, not on the tech.
Sound on videosLATERThe groovebox synth engine could score a clip.
FontsYESA fixed list of 42 pairings from free Google Fonts, built in. Fetched and cached on the web, bundled in the APK. No font management. Helvetica and Akzidenz stay out (licensed).
PalettesYESFixed list per style, light and dark. In Advanced you can edit the colours of the current design only.

06Reused from the earlier engine

No Shōmen branding. Only its visual elements carry over:

  • Marks: an optional layer of brackets, tick rulers, crosshair, slashes, barcode strip, status cells, micro labels and a chamfered card for the info slot. Off, light or full, over any style.
  • Finishes: Grunge from the Swiss recap look, plus VHS and Glitch. The effect passes never touch text.
  • Rules: spacing measured from real glyph edges, and the story zones you already use (text between y 260 and 1600).

07Plan

Revised 23 Nov, evening. Plug and play: fonts and palettes are fixed lists inside the app, nothing to manage. Own fonts, saved palettes and copy/paste of designs are out. Photo, export sizes and A3 print are in. In the repo since session 1 closed. This page lives there as docs/plan.html and each session updates its state.

Session 1 · the MVP · Done 23 Nov

Engine, colour, type, Simple mode

  • Spike rebuilt as layout → scene → paint, with a solver that rejects any layout where text overflows, overlaps or fails contrast.
  • Palettes as roles, each with a hand-made light and dark form.
  • 42 font pairings from free Google Fonts; a fourth seed for type.
  • Simple mode: Shuffle, Back, Keep, locks, text on/off, export and share in three sizes.
  • Open from this session: the online font checks could not run where it was built (Google Fonts was blocked there). They need one run on your computer; the backlog lists the commands under By hand.
Session 2 · Next

Swiss, Postmodern, finishes, marks

  • Both styles finished, with the variety rules at every level: layout (tilts, turns, depth, overlap), size (small to huge), graphics (bolder ranges, two or three approaches combined), and a check that a run of shuffles has no near-duplicates.
  • Postmodern gets two dialects: ice cream and photocopy grunge.
  • All four styles rebuilt as five separable parts, which is what makes the mix possible later.
  • Five finishes (Clean, Grain, Grunge, VHS, Glitch) and the marks layer.
Session 3 · Queued

Brutalist, Vaporwave, Advanced

  • Both styles finished from the first pass shown in 03, same variety rules.
  • Advanced mode: Layout, Graphic, Type, Colour, Text tabs with every parameter.
  • Colour tab: edit the 3–5 colours of the current design only. Nothing is saved to a library.
Session 4 · Queued

Photo and export

  • Upload one photo. Shuffle changes its crop, scale and placement with everything else.
  • Treatments: colour, monochrome, duotone from the palette, halftone, threshold, posterise, dither, plus the five finishes.
  • Export as JPEG, PNG or WebP at 1×, 2× or 3× (1080, 2160, 3240 px wide).
  • A fourth format, A (1:√2), with a print export: A3 at 300 dpi, 3508 × 4961 px, optional 3 mm bleed.
Session 5 · Queued

Text layers, then retouch

  • Add or remove text layers and give each a level: headline, subhead, body, label, caption. Replaces the four fixed slots.
  • Retouch from your notes.
Session 6 · experimental · Queued

Mix

  • Crosses of two styles: each of five parts (ground, layout, type, graphics, palette) comes from one parent. Advanced only.
  • Tuned pair by pair; pairs that only make mud are switched off.
Later

Motion

Needs its own spec first. MP4 test on your phone, then entrances and loops per style. Then the APK.

08Where it can go wrong

  • Random ≠ good. Some rolls are dull or clumsy. The fix is tighter rules and a "keep" pile, not more parameters. Expect a tuning pass per style.
  • Looks generic. A small graphics library gets recognisable fast. More motifs, the marks layer, per-design colour edits and your photo are what make outputs yours.
  • Phone limits. Two unknowns, both tested on your phone before anything depends on them: the 17-megapixel A3 render and MP4 export.
  • Scope creep. Every movement is tempting. Swiss alone has to be good before a third style exists.
